scope: Author-supplied read-only C28/C29 acceptance evidence mapping; not independent QA or a formal/general review

mapping.criterion: A valid --validate-install invokes compatible-host capability validation
mapping.established: The maintained fixture invocation succeeds with exit 0 and zero stdout/stderr on an installed PWA-shaped configuration. The compiled exact source reaches CheckCapability before returning 0.
mapping.limits: The Chrome proxy is an inert file and shell-link fixture, not an actually installed Chrome PWA; no unsupported-API or host-creation failure is injected.

mapping.criterion: Staged validation occurs before publication
mapping.established: A real staged installer invocation completes and its installed configuration and shortcut outputs are checked. Source orders its internal --validate-install before shortcut staging and Publish-LauncherArtifacts.
mapping.limits: The inner validator is not separately instrumented in the PowerShell child record. A CheckCapability failure preventing publication, and native failure-path ordering at that seam, are not directly observed.

mapping.criterion: Capability-API failure refuses installation without publishing
mapping.established: No retained native observation for this seam.
mapping.limits: Configuration/path/secret negative validations are different branches. Successful installer or attribute setup does not establish the failure branch.

mapping.criterion: Concurrent cold clicks and later warm PID reuse
mapping.established: Four concurrent native launch invocations all succeed quietly; lock PID equals the healthy gateway PID, a later click preserves health/PID, and the process remains live.
mapping.limits: A shared final PID and four successful clicks are observed; the test does not retain an OS-wide historical spawn count.

mapping.criterion: Provably different creation identity across directory/database locks and guards
mapping.established: The protected-PID case obtains actual CIM CreationDate as UTC FILETIME, seeds that identity minus 10000000 in all four paths, asserts direct helper state free and unchanged bytes for every fixture, then launches a different gateway and re-queries the original target identity unchanged.
mapping.limits: This is one joint four-path scenario, not four isolated path-specific records or per-query traces. The raw hosted log separately retains selected target identity; the typed artifact suppresses it.

mapping.criterion: Reused live PID in all four paths with concurrent cold clicks
mapping.established: All four paths are seeded with one old birth and token; two cold clicks complete; the new directory lock names the healthy gateway and has a non-old creation identity; the queried test process remains live.
mapping.limits: Only the new directory-lock PID/creation field is explicitly read back. This case alone does not compare the old birth to the original test process actual birth; use C29-different-four-paths for a provable native difference.

mapping.criterion: Matching creation identity on a valid database reclamation guard
mapping.established: Actual windowsProcessIdentity(process.pid) is validated; matching birth is written as a UUID marker in a physical database-guard directory; native launch refuses as store-held; marker bytes/log history remain unchanged and the queried test process remains live.
mapping.limits: This explicit matching-birth fixture covers the database guard, not every path.

mapping.criterion: Live owner of a shared database refuses a second launcher
mapping.established: A real running gateway owns the shared database; a different data directory/port using it is refused as store-held and the existing gateway still answers.
mapping.limits: No numeric creation-time equality is asserted/read back in this case. Calling it a matching-birth comparison requires the separately inspected common lock policy.

mapping.criterion: Matching live ownership on directory paths through API contenders
mapping.established: Three races have one live acquired API owner and four store-held refusals; recorded PID/token equal that owner and the old guard marker is absent.
mapping.limits: These are native API acquire calls, not launcher matching-birth fixtures. Neither a numeric matching creation-time field nor a separate directory-lock versus directory-guard refusal is retained. They do not complete the explicit matching matrix.

mapping.criterion: Missing stored creation identity for a live directory-lock PID
mapping.established: The pid-only fixture uses the live test PID with no windowsCreationTime in graphgoblin.lock. Native launch refuses store-unverified; bytes and prior gateway log remain identical; test PID survives.
mapping.limits: No equivalent PID-only valid directory guard/database lock/database guard case is asserted. Missing stored identity is not a native WMI query returning no identity.

mapping.criterion: Unverified or malformed records through the launcher
mapping.established: Malformed directory main record, PID4 without stored birth, and a file where a physical database guard directory is required each refuse store-unverified with bytes/log unchanged.
mapping.limits: PID4 has no stored birth, and file-guard is structurally invalid. Neither proves the valid-birth WMI unavailable/timeout/missing-result branch; valid directory-guard/database-lock variants remain uncovered.

mapping.criterion: Actual WMI query missing/unverified result for a valid stored creation identity
mapping.established: No such native observation in the maintained hosted corpus.
mapping.limits: At lines125-130 WMI is queried only for a valid stored birth. The PID-only/PID4 fixtures lack that birth. Individual four-path WMI timeout/failure/no-identity cases must remain uncovered.

mapping.criterion: Original record and marker bytes remain unchanged on refusal or read-only free check
mapping.established: The protected joint four-path direct helper free result preserves all seeded bytes; matching database marker, PID-only directory lock, PID4 record, malformed directory lock and invalid database guard bytes are re-read unchanged.
mapping.limits: The typed artifact does not contain raw stores; these observations bind through the exact passed case and assertion. They are not a live replacement-owner swap.

mapping.criterion: Original file identity under held retry
mapping.established: The controlled held helper scenarios preserve lock bytes and stat dev/ino, including stalled retry and held-to-free transition.
mapping.limits: The helper protocol is a disposable stub and the marker pid 1 is synthetic. This is original-file preservation, not real WMI or replacement-owner evidence.

mapping.criterion: New owner readback after stale-record recovery
mapping.established: Directory-lock readback names the new healthy gateway; API contention additionally reads the successful owner PID/token, checks stale marker absence, clean release and unrelated bytes.
mapping.limits: A newly acquired record replacing stale state is observed. This is not an adversarial live replacement while launcher refusal/cleanup is in progress, and no replacement file/guard inode is compared.

mapping.criterion: Replacement-owner record/file identity retained during helper refusal or cleanup
mapping.established: No maintained test deliberately swaps a live owner record/guard during that window and asserts replacement token, bytes and file identity.
mapping.limits: Original-file preservation and post-reclamation owner PID/token checks do not establish this race.

mapping.criterion: Queried process survives collection/refusal
mapping.established: The protected queried process creation identity is re-read equal after launch; fixture test PID liveness is checked after each matching/unknown refusal and reused-PID case.
mapping.limits: Protected target birth equality is stronger than PID-only liveness. The maintained corpus does not witness the WMI service or provider sessions.

mapping.criterion: Closed and bounded text supplied to dialog renderer
mapping.established: Compiled NativeChecks invokes production Program.Present and RenderPath; asserts no raw canary, valid configuration location, safe path truncation, and helper-failure canary exclusion.
mapping.limits: These are executed managed presentation/string assertions in a native C# process, not a visible MessageBox observation.

mapping.criterion: Native error dialog rendering, including oversized/flood cases
mapping.established: No MessageBox display is exercised and inspected in the retained maintained tests.
mapping.limits: --ensure-gateway makes failure paths quiet. Other HWND/COM Form tests do not inspect the error dialog. Managed text checks must not be upgraded to native dialog acceptance.

mapping.criterion: Store-unverified refusal through the launcher
mapping.established: Typed launcher diagnostics record store-unverified for malformed, PID-only, PID4 and invalid-guard scenarios.
mapping.limits: Covers these reasons only; not an actual failed WMI query with a valid stored birth.

mapping.criterion: Store-acquiring outcome through the launcher
mapping.established: No child observation has diagnostic store-acquiring. Maintained source has no targeted native acquiring-output assertion.
mapping.limits: A live guard yielding store-held and contender acquisition do not prove this distinct launcher outcome.

mapping.criterion: Supported Windows Server runner observation
mapping.established: The verified Windows job ran on Microsoft Windows Server 2025 Datacenter 10.0.26100, image windows-2025-vs2026 version 20261116.315.1; manifest binds Windows/X64 and Node v22.23.5.
mapping.limits: One Server 2025 runner/image is observed. This does not establish every supported Windows/Server release or restrictive host policy.

mapping.criterion: Fresh-runner measurements and boot provenance
mapping.established: The retained job is a hosted server-image execution with per-child timings and a fresh checkout binding.
mapping.limits: No boot-age or first-WMI-use witness exists. Do not upgrade runner-image metadata or first recorded helper to cold-WMI provenance.

mapping.criterion: First WMI use after boot
mapping.established: No maintained observation establishes first-use-after-boot.
mapping.limits: Preserve C30 LIMIT. Existing native timings are fresh-process observations with prior WMI use unknown.

mapping.criterion: WMI service and provider-session survival outside helper job
mapping.established: No maintained observation records WMI-service/provider exact handles or job membership.
mapping.limits: Protected queried process survival does not identify the WMI service. No new enumeration was run for this mapping.

matching: native API held-owner contention only; no separate numeric-birth comparison or path discriminator
native launcher live-database-held refusal; numeric equality inferred only from common policy
explicit actual-birth fixture and held refusal
